h1: La Plagne ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: La Plagne spreads across a mountainside at around 2,000 metres with 225 kilometres of pistes beneath and above it, running from 1,250 metres up to a glacier at 3,080 - a crossing of every Alpine layer, as the operator puts it, from dolines and forest to ice. Fifty-two of its runs are graded red or black, and the season runs 12 December 2026 to 24 April 2027.
stayOverview: Plagne Altitude is the cluster of purpose-built villages high on the mountain; Montalbert, Champagny-en-Vanoise and Montchavin - Les Coches sit lower in the trees and run their own season dates.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. The altitude villages are ski-in; the lower ones are cheaper and keep their trees.
rentalCars: La Plagne is reached from Aime or Bourg-Saint-Maurice in the Tarentaise, about two and a half hours from Geneva.

lifts.unannounced: No lift count is published on the operator's ski-area pages.

verticalDrop.unannounced: The operator publishes an altitude range of 1,250 m to 3,080 m but no vertical drop; subtracting the two would be our arithmetic.

season.note: Plagne Altitude. The lower villages - Montalbert, Champagny-en-Vanoise and Montchavin-Les Coches - run to 17 April 2027.

baseElevation.note: The operator gives La Plagne as 1,250 to 3,080 m; the wider Paradiski area it belongs to runs 1,200 to 3,250 m.

longestRun.unannounced: The operator publishes the altitude range, 225 km of pistes and the count of red and black runs, but names no longest run - only the funslope, which it calls Europe's longest without giving a length.

dayPass.note: A La Plagne day pass midweek. The resort publishes separate early and late-season and weekend offers, and sends Paradiski day-pass buyers to its booking site.
